input.findings_json:
[
  {
    "file": "shopapi/auth.py",
    "line": 55,
    "category": "Authentication",
    "title": "Authentication failures are swallowed, allowing protected handlers to run unauthenticated",
    "description": "require_auth catches all exceptions, including the 401 abort it raises when no valid user is present, then invokes the wrapped handler with g.user set to None. Any protected handler that does not immediately dereference g.user can therefore execute without authentication.",
    "evidence": "The wrapper catches abort(401) at lines 51-57 and calls the handler at line 58 regardless. GET /orders/3 without an Authorization header returned HTTP 200 and disclosed the order because show_order only uses the path ID."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/orders.py",
    "line": 49,
    "category": "Access control",
    "title": "Order detail does not enforce ownership",
    "description": "The order-detail endpoint calls get_order rather than own_order, so an authenticated customer (and, due to the authentication failure bug, an unauthenticated caller) can retrieve another customer's order details.",
    "evidence": "GET /orders/3 with Priya's token returned Tom's order, including items, payment amount, delivery date, and refunds. The vulnerable path is show_order -> get_order at shopapi/orders.py:48-49; own_order is not called."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/auth.py",
    "line": 101,
    "category": "Authentication",
    "title": "Token refresh accepts unsigned JWT claims",
    "description": "The refresh endpoint disables signature verification and uses the unverified sub claim to select an account before issuing a newly signed token. An attacker can forge a token naming another user, including a staff user.",
    "evidence": "refresh calls jwt.decode(token, options={\"verify_signature\": False}) at line 101, then load_user(claims.get(\"sub\")) and make_token. A forged unsigned JWT with sub=3 was accepted by POST /auth/refresh and returned a valid token for the staff account."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/basket.py",
    "line": 20,
    "category": "Deserialization",
    "title": "Unauthenticated basket cookie permits arbitrary pickle deserialization",
    "description": "The basket cookie is client-controlled and has no signature or MAC, but is passed to pickle.loads. A crafted cookie can execute attacker-controlled Python when an endpoint reads the basket.",
    "evidence": "read_basket base64-decodes the request cookie and calls pickle.loads at line 20; with_basket creates the cookie without integrity protection at line 27. GET /basket reads the cookie without authentication."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/__init__.py",
    "line": 37,
    "category": "Access control",
    "title": "Trailing-slash admin refund route bypasses staff authorization",
    "description": "The staff hook compares request.path to the set of registered rule strings. The refund route accepts both slash variants with strict_slashes=False, but the alternate trailing-slash path is not matched, so it reaches the staff-only handler without a role check.",
    "evidence": "POST /admin/refunds/ without Authorization and with an order_id and amount returned HTTP 200 and performed a refund. The route is declared at shopapi/admin.py:52 with strict_slashes=False, while the hook uses exact request.path membership at line 37."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/products.py",
    "line": 41,
    "category": "SQL injection",
    "title": "Product search concatenates the query directly into SQL",
    "description": "The q parameter is concatenated into a SQL LIKE expression rather than bound as a parameter, allowing an attacker to alter the predicate and retrieve unintended records.",
    "evidence": "GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201=1-- returned all six products. The statement at lines 40-41 directly concatenates q into both LIKE clauses."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/admin.py",
    "line": 80,
    "category": "SQL injection",
    "title": "Customer display names enable second-order SQL injection in the staff report",
    "description": "The review report interpolates a mutable customer display_name into SQL. A customer can set a display name containing SQL syntax, and a staff member later viewing that customer's report executes the injected query.",
    "evidence": "PATCH /account stores display_name from the request using a parameterized update at auth.py:116-125, but admin.py:77-80 constructs `WHERE r.author_name = '{customer['display_name']}'` with an f-string and no SQL parameterization."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/templates/product.html",
    "line": 13,
    "category": "Cross-site scripting",
    "title": "Review bodies are rendered as trusted HTML",
    "description": "Review bodies are accepted without sanitization and rendered with Jinja's safe filter. A malicious authenticated customer can store script markup that executes for visitors viewing the product page.",
    "evidence": "POST /products/<product_id>/reviews stores body directly at products.py:90-91, and the product template renders `r.body|safe` at line 13."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/payments.py",
    "line": 42,
    "category": "Business logic",
    "title": "Payment timeout fails open and marks orders paid",
    "description": "A timeout while checking the payment provider is treated as a successful payment. The order is then changed to processing and paid_pence is set to the full total without provider confirmation.",
    "evidence": "confirm_payment catches requests.Timeout at lines 39-42 and sets status = \"paid\`; lines 43-45 then update the order to processing and set paid_pence = total_pence."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/payments.py",
    "line": 70,
    "category": "Integrity",
    "title": "Payment webhook does not validate the paid amount or sign the event contents",
    "description": "A webhook signature covers only order_id. If the secret is known or the provider is compromised, an event with status paid and an arbitrary amount, including zero, transitions the complete order to processing without comparing the amount to the order total.",
    "evidence": "webhook_signature at lines 53-55 signs only order_id. Lines 69-71 accept status paid and store int(event.get(\"amount_pence\", 0)) without comparing it with order['total_pence']."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/payments.py",
    "line": 23,
    "category": "Business logic",
    "title": "External refunds are not atomic with local refund records",
    "description": "issue_refund calls the payment provider before inserting the local refund record, and callers commit only afterward. A database failure after provider success leaves local state inconsistent; retrying can issue duplicate refunds or exceed intended refund totals.",
    "evidence": "payments.py:21-23 calls client().refund before the INSERT, while orders.py:69-71 and admin.py:65-66 commit afterward. No idempotency key or reconciliation path is present."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/giftcards.py",
    "line": 39,
    "category": "Business logic",
    "title": "Concurrent gift-card redemptions can double spend a balance",
    "description": "The balance check, derived new balance, redemption insert, and balance update are not protected by a row lock or atomic conditional update. Concurrent requests can both validate against the same balance, create multiple redemptions, and reduce an order more than the card's available value.",
    "evidence": "The handler checks card balance at line 39, computes new_balance at line 41, inserts the redemption at line 42, and updates the card at line 43. There is no transaction locking or `WHERE balance_pence >= amount` condition."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/orders.py",
    "line": 65,
    "category": "Business logic",
    "title": "Concurrent cancellations and returns can issue duplicate refunds",
    "description": "Cancellation and return quantities are checked and incremented in separate statements, then refunded. Concurrent requests can both pass the remaining-quantity check and refund more units than the order contains.",
    "evidence": "cancel_items checks cancelled_qty at line 65, updates it at line 67, and refunds at line 70; return_items performs the analogous sequence at lines 91-96. Neither uses row locking or an atomic conditional update."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/auth.py",
    "line": 16,
    "category": "Cryptography",
    "title": "Passwords are stored with unsalted SHA-256",
    "description": "Passwords use a single fast unsalted SHA-256 digest instead of a password-specific hashing scheme such as Argon2id, scrypt, or bcrypt. A database compromise therefore enables efficient offline cracking.",
    "evidence": "hash_password returns hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest() at lines 15-16, and the digest is stored during registration and reset."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/auth.py",
    "line": 135,
    "category": "Authentication",
    "title": "Password reset codes use weak randomness and have no guessing or request limits",
    "description": "Reset codes are eight decimal digits generated with the non-cryptographic random module, remain valid for 30 minutes, and have no failed-attempt counter or endpoint throttling. An attacker can repeatedly guess codes or repeatedly trigger reset messages.",
    "evidence": "Codes are generated with random.random at line 135 and expire after 30 minutes at lines 136-137. reset_confirm compares the supplied code at line 153 without recording failures, and neither reset endpoint implements rate limiting."
  },
  {
    "file": "config.py",
    "line": 3,
    "category": "Cryptography",
    "title": "JWT signing key is hardcoded and weak",
    "description": "The HS256 signing key is a short static repository value. Anyone obtaining the source or deployment artifact can forge access tokens, including staff tokens.",
    "evidence": "config.py defines SECRET_KEY = \"hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d\" at line 3; auth.py uses it for both signing and verification at lines 27 and 42."
  },
  {
    "file": "config.py",
    "line": 8,
    "category": "Cryptography",
    "title": "Webhook signing secret has a predictable default",
    "description": "When WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, the application uses the repository-visible value whsec-local. A reachable webhook can therefore be forged in deployments that rely on the default.",
    "evidence": "config.py line 8 uses os.environ.get(\"WEBHOOK_SECRET\", \"whsec-local\"), and payments.py uses this value to verify X-Signature."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/__init__.py",
    "line": 31,
    "category": "Logging",
    "title": "Request logging records credentials and sensitive request bodies",
    "description": "The global request hook logs the body of every POST, PUT, and PATCH request, including login passwords, reset codes, payment data, and customer information. These values can persist in application logs accessible to operators or log aggregation systems.",
    "evidence": "shopapi/__init__.py:29-31 logs request.get_data(as_text=True)[:2000] before routing. Login and password-reset endpoints send secrets in these bodies."
  },
  {
    "file": "run.py",
    "line": 6,
    "category": "Configuration",
    "title": "Application entry point enables Flask debug mode",
    "description": "The executable entry point starts Flask with debug=True. If run.py is used in a reachable deployment, unhandled exceptions expose debug behavior and potentially the interactive debugger.",
    "evidence": "run.py line 6 calls app.run(..., debug=True)."
  },
  {
    "file": "requirements.txt",
    "line": 1,
    "category": "Dependencies and build",
    "title": "Mixed private and public indexes create dependency-confusion risk",
    "description": "Installation uses a private index as the primary index and PyPI as an extra index. If a package expected from the private repository is missing or resolution is misconfigured, a public package with the same name can enter the production build.",
    "evidence": "requirements.txt lines 1-2 configure an internal --index-url and public --extra-index-url; the production install resolves packages across both indexes."
  }
]
